subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should OpenClaw support cleanup-by-default for recurring isolated cron jobs, or keep `deleteAfterRun` as a one-shot-only lifecycle contract and reject recurring uses?
rationale: The linked fix and the competing open PR encode opposite product contracts, and the choice affects persisted cron state, session cleanup, and user upgrade behavior.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR direction, but require an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Pause or close this PR in favor of strict validation after its Gateway/UI/recovery blockers are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land only the new-create default and document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR direction, but require an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron store migration/default semantics and product compatibility, and @steipete has recent history in that store boundary.
